In order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion, I have taken all these points together for common consideration for the sake of brevity.
PW1 Ranjitha being the first informant has deposed that her marriage with accused No.1 was took place on 30-12-2015 at Shivamogga.

That accused No.1 demanded her to bring  3,00,000/- for purchase of site and 35,000/- for Honda Activa, she gave  35,000/-
through her uncle.

sentences.text: During the cross examination of advocate for accused PW4 admitted that his first wife was committed suicide in the year 2016 thereafter he got performed second marriage with a woman of Koolambi village of Honnali Taluk.
He also admitted that the parents of his first wife has lodged case against him in that case he was absconding for 6 months.

He denied the suggestion that during that time accused No.1 not allowed him to stay in his house, as such on that  17 C.C.No.18308/2019 grudge he got filed a false case through PW1 against accused and was deposing falsely.
He denied all other suggestions put to him.

20. PW5 Ravi being the HC of Bommanahalli PS has deposed that on 19-02-2019 PW1 came to police station and lodged first information as per Ex.P1, on the basis of which he registered the Cr.No.48/2019 and issued F.I.R.
as per Ex.P3 and handed over the case to PW6 for further investigation.

21. PW6 D.R.Nagaraj being the Investigation Officer has deposed that on 22-02-2019 he received the case file from PW5, at about 11.00 a.m., he visited the spot and conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 as shown by PW1 in the presence of CW2 and PW2 and recorded the statements of witnesses.

Thereafter he received marriage photographs,

sentences.text: That after completion of investigation he filed the charge sheet against the accused persons.
22. During cross-examination, PW6 stated that he has not inquired the owner of the house where accused No.1 and PW1 were residing as well as neighbours.
He admitted that Ex.P9 is in the name of aunt of PW1 but he has not taken the statement of said Shivakumari.

PW5 and 6 have denied the suggestion that though accused have not committed any offences as alleged, only as per the say of PW1 and their parents, they have registered false case and filed false charge sheet against the accused persons.
23. In this case, except the relatives of PW1 no other independent witnesses were examined by the prosecution.

Though PW1 being the first informant as well as victim deposed against the accused but during cross examination she has categorically admitted that accused No.2 who was  19 C.C.No.18308/2019 aged about 70 years, accused No.4 was aged about 85 years and accused No.3 was died due to old age ailments and accused No.2 to 4 were residing at Davanagere from the inception.

These admissions clearly goes to show that accused No.2 to 4 never residing with PW1 and accused Smt Ranjitha vs Arunkumar on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30311751/
12 No.1 at Benglauru due to their age as well as ill health.
Under such circumstances, the question of demanding the dowry as alleged by the prosecution is appears to be doubtful.
24.

It is also material to mention here that initially PW1 has categorically stated that she does not know where she puts her signature on Ex.P2 spot mahazar and police have not conducted any spot mahazar in her presence.
Thereafter, the learned Sr.APP by treating her partly hostile her and cross examined her then only she admitted about conducting of spot mahazar as per Ex.P2.

If at all the spot  20 C.C.No.18308/2019 mahazar as per the case of prosecution has been conducted at the spot she would have definitely stated about the conducting of spot mahazar in her presence so it appears that the spot mahazar has not been conducted at the spot therefore the PW1 has not stated about the same during her examination in chief.
25.

Though PW2 being the witness to the spot mahazar has stated about conducting of spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 at the spot but he has clearly admitted during cross examination that he does not know the reason for the quarrel between accused and PW1.

Therefore, on consideration of the admission of PW2 along with the Smt Ranjitha vs Arunkumar on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30311751/
13 evidence of PW1 it clearly goes to show that the prosecution has failed to prove the spot mahazar as per law.

The PW3 being the brother and PW4 being the uncle of PW1 have also stated in the same line as of PW1, but except the family members of PW1 no independent witnesses were either cited or examined by the prosecution.

It is interesting to note here that PW6 being the investigating officer has categorically admitted that he has neither inquired the owner of the house where PW1 and accused were residing nor taken statements of the neighbours of the said house.

It is needless to say that to corroborate the version of PW1 the evidence of neighbours is very material to prove the alleged cruelty given by the accused against the PW1.
27.
On meticulous consideration of the entire evidence available on record except the relatives of PW1 no independent witness is examined.
Even the prosecution has failed to prove the spot mahazar as discussed above.

22 C.C.No.18308/2019 Though PW3 and 4 being the brother and maternal uncle of PW1 have deposed as per the case of the prosecution,
but they are residing at Davanagere District and at the most they are termed as hear say witnesses but the Smt Ranjitha vs Arunkumar on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30311751/
14 absence of the eye witness or neighbouring witnesses their evidence will not get any credence.
The contention of the advocate for accused is having substance that they are all interested witnesses.
28. Though PW5 and 6 being the official witnesses have stated the case of the prosecution.
They being the investigation officers have stated about their role during the investigation.
But only on the basis of their evidence the accused cannot be held guilty for the alleged offences.

29. As per the prosecution the alleged offence took place on 20-01-2019 where as the first information has been lodged on 19.02.2019 so there is a delay of one month  23 C.C.No.18308/2019 which was not property explained.
Moreover in Ex.P1 the first information statement the date has been typed as 18.02.2019 at page No.4, whereas in the first page of the same the date was written as 19-02-2019.
So also the Ex.P1 was registered on 19-02-2019.
The Ex.P1 contains 4 pages that too at the last page after the typed matter 4 lines were written by hand by adding the names of accused No.2 to 4.
This also fortify the contention of the advocate for the accused that intentionally in order to harass the accused they were falsely implicated in this case.

So, on perusal of these things the first information statement Smt Ranjitha vs Arunkumar on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30311751/
15 itself creates a serious doubt with regard to case of the prosecution.
30. Looking to the entire oral as well as documentary evidence placed on record, I am of the considered opinion that they are not enough to bring home the guilt of the accused persons.
Under such circumstances, I have no  24 C.C.No.18308/2019 hesitation to arrive at a conclusion that the prosecution is not successful in proving its case against accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, as per the settled principle of law the benefit of doubt has to be extended to accused persons.
In the result, I answer the above points in the negative.
31. Point No.4:-

For the forgoing reasons and my findings to the above points, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER Accused No.1, 2 & 4 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/sec.498(A) r/w 34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of D.P. Act, by acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C.
Their bail bonds stand cancelled.
However, in view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C the same shall be in force for 6 (six) months.

On meticulous consideration of the entire evidence available on record except the relatives of PW1 no independent witness is examined.
Even the prosecution has failed to prove the spot mahazar as discussed above.
But only on the basis of their evidence the accused cannot be held guilty for the alleged offences.
Under such circumstances, I have no  24 C.C.No.18308/2019 hesitation to arrive at a conclusion that the prosecution is not successful in proving its case against accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, as per the settled principle of law the benefit of doubt has to be extended to accused persons.
